pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FRIENDLY LETTER

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do you communicat e with people who are far away?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the components of a friendly letter from a sample letter
2. write a friendly letter using the correct format for effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the components of a friendly letter from a sample letter.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you communicat e with people who are far away?
2. Why do we write letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
